shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor (GIST)
shortlist.why_kept: submucosal mass with vascular signal on imaging

shortlist.label: Leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: submucosal mass with normal overlying mucosa

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: submucosal mass with potential for malignancy

shortlist.label: Dieulafoy's lesion
shortlist.why_kept: intermittent gastrointestinal bleeding with normal overlying mucosa

raw.rationale: The presence of a submucosal mass with normal overlying mucosa, a low-echo lesion with regular margins on endoscopic ultrasound, and a vascular signal on color Doppler imaging are characteristic of GIST. The size and location of the mass, as well as the absence of lymphadenopathy, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Leiomyoma
rejected.why: Leiomyomas are typically smaller and less likely to cause significant bleeding or anemia.

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: Leiomyosarcomas are rare and usually present with more aggressive features, such as invasion into surrounding tissues or lymphadenopathy, which are not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Gastric adenocarcinoma typically presents with mucosal ulceration or irregularity, which is not present in this case, and often has lymphadenopathy or distant metastasis.

rejected.label: Dieulafoy's lesion
rejected.why: Dieulafoy's lesion is a small, superficial lesion that causes bleeding due to an exposed artery, which does not match the large submucosal mass described in this case.
